plants.name: Haworthia attenuata
plants.tip: Tolerates a shadier spot than most succulents, but water it the same there and the roots rot.
plants.colour: Dark green pointed leaves banded with raised white tubercles

plants.name: Haworthia attenuata 'Variegata'
plants.tip: The cream sectors carry no chlorophyll and scorch first. Keep it off a hot midday windowsill.
plants.colour: Green and white tubercled leaves with broad cream longitudinal stripes

plants.name: Haworthia attenuata var. radula
plants.tip: The fine tubercles trap dust. Rinse the leaves under a tap and let it dry before watering.
plants.colour: Slender dark green leaves peppered with many small white dots

plants.name: Haworthia fasciata
plants.tip: Water into the compost, not the rosette. Water left sitting in the centre rots the growing point.
plants.colour: Thick dark green leaves with white banding on the undersides only

plants.name: Haworthia fasciata 'Big Band'
plants.tip: The broad banding fades in a dim corner. A bright sill through winter keeps the contrast.
plants.colour: Dark green leaves crossed by unusually wide chalk-white bands

plants.name: Haworthia limifolia
plants.tip: The ridges show best on a lean plant. Rich compost and heavy feeding give soft, flat, unmarked leaves.
plants.colour: Deep green triangular leaves with concentric raised ridges

plants.name: Haworthia limifolia var. striata
plants.tip: Grows slowly and resents disturbance. Leave it potted for three years and only refresh the top layer.
plants.colour: Olive leaves with pale raised ridges running the length of the leaf

plants.name: Haworthia limifolia 'Spider White'
plants.tip: The white areas burn in direct sun. Bright shade keeps the marking and stops the tips going papery.
plants.colour: Ridged green leaves overlaid with irregular chalky white variegation

plants.name: Haworthia coarctata
plants.tip: The stem lengthens until it topples. Cut the top off, dry the wound a week, then root it as a new plant.
plants.colour: Columns of overlapping green leaves studded with white tubercles

plants.name: Haworthia coarctata var. adelaidensis
plants.tip: Leaves flush red-brown under strong light and that is normal. Real burn shows as dry white patches.
plants.colour: Stacked leaves turning bronze to red-brown in strong light

plants.name: Haworthia reinwardtii
plants.tip: Stems flop once they pass a hand's length. Stake them or take cuttings; a sprawling column rarely re-roots.
plants.colour: Slim upright columns of incurved leaves dotted with white

plants.name: Haworthia scabra
plants.tip: Almost stops growing in summer heat. Hold back water through the hottest weeks and resume when nights cool.
plants.colour: Stiff dark olive leaves with a rough sandpaper surface

plants.name: Haworthia viscosa
plants.tip: The three ranks of leaves need light from all sides. Turn the pot a quarter each week or it grows lopsided.
plants.colour: Three ranks of stacked triangular leaves in dull green to bronze

plants.name: Haworthia tessellata
plants.tip: The leaf windows work like panels. Let them get dusty or buried and the plant stretches and loses its pattern.
plants.colour: Flat green leaves with a fine chequered pattern of translucent veining

plants.name: Haworthia nigra
plants.tip: Goes near-black in strong light and dull green in shade. Move it gradually; a sudden shift scorches it.
plants.colour: Very dark grey-green tubercled leaves in three stacked ranks

plants.name: Haworthia koelmaniorum
plants.tip: Slow even by Haworthia standards. Repot only when roots fill the pot, and never into anything much larger.
plants.colour: Broad rough-textured leaves in brown-green with paler tubercles

plants.name: Haworthia venosa
plants.tip: Spreads by underground runners and fills a shallow pot. Split the clump every second spring.
plants.colour: Blunt green leaves with a net of translucent veins on the upper face

plants.name: Haworthia pumila
plants.tip: The largest of the group and heavy once watered. A clay pot stops it tipping and dries the compost faster.
plants.colour: Large dark green rosette covered in pearly raised white tubercles

plants.name: Haworthia marginata
plants.tip: The smooth leaves show every mark. Handle it by the pot, as fingernail dents never grow out.
plants.colour: Glossy hard dark green leaves with pale horny margins

plants.name: Haworthia minima
plants.tip: Offsets slowly and takes years to reach size. Buy the size you want rather than expecting quick growth.
plants.colour: Blue-grey pointed leaves with scattered white tubercles

plants.name: Haworthia blackburniae
plants.tip: Grassy leaves over a thick tuberous root. It stores water underground, so water less than the foliage suggests.
plants.colour: Long trailing grass-like green leaves from a swollen root

plants.name: Haworthia cooperi
plants.tip: The translucent leaf tips go cloudy when it is thirsty and plump again after a soak. Use them as the gauge.
plants.colour: Pale green rosette of swollen leaves with clear glassy tips

plants.name: Haworthia cooperi var. truncata
plants.tip: The flat leaf tops sit at soil level in habitat. Top-dress with grit so the leaves rest on it, not on compost.
plants.colour: Tight cluster of blunt-tipped leaves with flat translucent windows

plants.name: Haworthia cooperi var. pilifera
plants.tip: The fine bristles on the leaf tips break off if handled. Water from below to keep the rosette dry.
plants.colour: Soft green windowed leaves each ending in a fine white bristle

plants.name: Haworthia cooperi var. obtusa
plants.tip: The plump leaves split if watered heavily after a dry spell. Bring it back into growth gradually.
plants.colour: Rounded bubble-like leaves in pale green with clear tops

plants.name: Haworthia cymbiformis
plants.tip: Offsets fast and crowds itself out. Divide it every other spring or the central rosette starves.
plants.colour: Boat-shaped light green leaves with translucent striped tips

plants.name: Haworthia cymbiformis 'Variegata'
plants.tip: Reverted all-green offsets grow faster and take over. Remove them as soon as they appear at the base.
plants.colour: Pale green boat-shaped leaves striped lengthways in cream and yellow

plants.name: Haworthia retusa
plants.tip: Leaves lie flat and face upward in good light. In poor light they stretch upright, and that never reverses.
plants.colour: Fat triangular leaves with flat upper windows lined in green

plants.name: Haworthia magnifica
plants.tip: The rough grey leaf surface marks permanently from water spots. Water the compost and keep the rosette dry.
plants.colour: Dark grey-green leaves with a rough matt surface and pale flecks

plants.name: Haworthia turgida
plants.tip: Forms mats of small rosettes that hide rot beneath them. Lift the clump each spring and check the base.
plants.colour: Clustering pale green rosettes with keeled translucent leaf tips

plants.name: Haworthia mirabilis
plants.tip: Rests through high summer. Watering it while dormant in the hottest weeks is the usual way this one dies.
plants.colour: Green leaves flushing purple-brown with pale window margins

plants.name: Haworthia emelyae
plants.tip: The windowed leaf faces need light from above. Under a shelf it stretches and the pattern flattens out.
plants.colour: Rough brown-green leaf faces marked with pale reticulated lines

plants.name: Haworthia emelyae var. major
plants.tip: The bristly leaf faces collect grit from top-dressing. Blow it out; picking it off tears the leaf skin.
plants.colour: Bristle-edged olive leaves with a coarse pitted upper surface

plants.name: Haworthia bayeri
plants.tip: Very slow and very rot-prone. Grow it in pure pumice or grit and water only once the leaves soften.
plants.colour: Dark leaf faces patterned with a fine pale translucent net

plants.name: Haworthia springbokvlakensis
plants.tip: Grows almost buried in habitat. Pot it deep in grit and expect only the leaf windows to show at the surface.
plants.colour: Blunt rounded leaves with large dull translucent windows

plants.name: Haworthia pygmaea
plants.tip: The frosted leaf surface is the plant's own sunscreen. Wiping it off leaves the leaf open to scorching.
plants.colour: Small green rosette with a frosted sugary coating on the leaf faces

plants.name: Haworthia pygmaea var. splendens
plants.tip: The leaf pattern only develops with age. Give it years of steady light and leave it in the same pot.
plants.colour: Broad leaf faces in bronze and green with raised pale markings

plants.name: Haworthia truncata
plants.tip: Deep roots want a tall pot. In a shallow one they circle and the fan of leaves never widens properly.
plants.colour: Two ranks of upright leaves cut flat across the top like teeth

plants.name: Haworthia maughanii
plants.tip: Grown for the flat leaf faces, so keep top-dressing grit off them and let them see the light.
plants.colour: Round cluster of cylindrical leaves with flat translucent tops

plants.name: Haworthia arachnoidea
plants.tip: The white bristles hold water against the leaves. Water at the base only and never leave it damp overnight.
plants.colour: Pale green rosette wrapped in a web of long white marginal bristles

plants.name: Haworthia semiviva
plants.tip: Looks dead through summer, which is simply its dormancy. Leave the dry outer leaves on as shade for the centre.
plants.colour: Grey-white rosette buried under papery dried outer leaves

plants.name: Haworthia cuspidata
plants.tip: A garden hybrid and tougher than either parent, but it still rots if left wet through a cold week.
plants.colour: Pale green star-shaped rosette with keeled semi-translucent leaves
